title: The Nancy Pelosi / Paul Pelosi household trades using non-public information
short_summary: Public PTRs document large, repeated trades by the Pelosi household in major tech names. A large retail copycat/tracker ecosystem exists. No specific non-public-information to specific-trade chain has been established. Label remains Contested.
label: Contested
residual_note: Primary missing link remains specific non-public info to specific trade.
evidence_for: Official House PTRs document large repeated trades in major tech names including options.
Dedicated Pelosi trackers, copy-trading apps, and the NANC ETF treat disclosed activity as a signal.
evidence_against: No criminal conviction, SEC action, or formal STOCK Act finding specific to these trades.
Aggregate post-STOCK Act academic work does not support a reliable market-beating congressional edge.

title: Members of Congress systematically trade securities using non-public information
short_summary: High trade volume and sector-jurisdiction overlaps are documented for multiple members. Systematic use of non-public information across Congress remains Contested.
label: Contested
evidence_for: Public PTR rankings show high trade counts for multiple members.
Committee jurisdiction plus sector overlap strengthens appearance for some names.
evidence_against: High volume does not equal use of non-public information.
No systematic set of specific-info to specific-trade chains established in open sources.

title: The STOCK Act is inadequate — late filings are common and real enforcement is rare
short_summary: Late filings under the STOCK Act are relatively common; baseline late fee is low; formal public sanctions are rare. Late-filing pattern and rare formal penalties are True.
label: True
evidence_for: Late filings are relatively common in ethics-watchdog summaries.
Statutory late fee starts around $200; formal public sanctions remain rare.
House passed H.R. 7008 (Stop Insider Trading Act) 22 Jul 2026.
evidence_against: STOCK Act did create a legal duty and public disclosure system that did not exist before 2012.
Rare formal penalties does not by itself prove widespread serious violations.

title: After the STOCK Act, members of Congress as a class do not beat the market on aggregate
short_summary: Post-STOCK Act academic work finds no reliable evidence of superior aggregate performance by members once controls are applied. Label: Likely but Unproven.
label: Likely but Unproven
evidence_for: Belmont et al. 2022: no evidence of superior aggregate performance.
Chen and Sacerdote NBER 2026: portfolios underperform or match benchmarks.
evidence_against: Single-name tracker narratives can still look spectacular.
Upper percentiles of returns can be consistent with random picking.

title: Jeffrey Epstein
short_summary: American financier and convicted sex offender. Central figure in a long-running sex-trafficking operation involving underage girls. 2008 Florida plea; 2019 federal indictment; died in custody 10 Aug 2019 (official ruling: suicide).
label: True
residual_note: Core criminal facts True. Alternative death explanations Contested and held in Case portfolio.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell
short_summary: British former socialite and long-time associate of Jeffrey Epstein. Convicted 2021 on five federal counts related to sex trafficking of minors; sentenced to 20 years. Direct appeals exhausted.
label: True

title: Little St. James (Epstein Island)
short_summary: Small private island in the U.S. Virgin Islands owned by Jeffrey Epstein. Most frequently cited physical location in court records for alleged trafficking and abuse activities.
label: True

title: Bill Clinton
short_summary: 42nd President of the United States (1993-2001). Founder of the Clinton Foundation network. Documented association with Jeffrey Epstein via flight logs (2002-2003, about 26 legs / 4 trips).
label: True
residual_note: Epstein flight association True; island visits Unsupported.

title: Hillary Clinton
short_summary: First Lady; U.S. Senator (NY); 67th Secretary of State (2009-2013); 2016 Democratic nominee. Central figure in Clinton Foundation donor controversies during State tenure.
label: True

title: Clinton Foundations
short_summary: Post-presidency philanthropic network founded by Bill Clinton (2001). Accepted foreign-government donations including during Hillary Clinton State tenure under a 2008 ethics MOU.
label: True

title: Uranium One / Rosatom acquisition and Clinton Foundation flows
short_summary: Rosatom acquired controlling interest in Uranium One via CFIUS review. State was a CFIUS member. Giustra and others donated to Clinton vehicles; Bill Clinton received a $500k Moscow speech fee. Strong quid-pro-quo framing is Contested/False as stated.
label: Contested
evidence_for: Rosatom acquired controlling interest in Uranium One; CFIUS reviewed and did not block.
Bill Clinton received $500,000 from Renaissance Capital for a Moscow speech (29 Jun 2010).
evidence_against: CFIUS is multi-agency; only the President holds veto power; no primary document of personal decision authority.
No primary document establishing a quid-pro-quo agreement has entered the public record reviewed.

title: Candace Owens
